skill.description: Guides developers through building ChatGPT Apps with interactive widgets, FastMCP servers, response metadata, and Developer Mode setup.
skill.summary: Build ChatGPT Apps with interactive widgets, FastMCP server templates, response metadata, and debugging guidance.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily documentation and sample templates for building ChatGPT Apps, and most static findings are false positives from markdown code fences, URLs, or CSS text. The real risks are development guidance that binds a server to all interfaces, exposes it through ngrok without authentication, and uses forceful process-kill commands during cache resets.

remediation.issue: Development templates expose the MCP server on all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Default examples to localhost for local development and add a warning before any 0.0.0.0 binding.

remediation.issue: The workflow shows public ngrok registration with no authentication.
remediation.suggestion: State that No Auth is only for local prototypes and require authentication before handling user or production data.

remediation.issue: Cache reset instructions use forceful process termination.
remediation.suggestion: Replace kill -9 pipelines with safer commands that show the target process and ask for confirmation before termination.

content.value_statement: Building ChatGPT Apps requires specific widget metadata, server structure, and testing steps. This skill provides templates and guidance for creating interactive Apps with MCP servers and embedded widgets.
actual_capabilities: Explains the window.openai widget APIs for follow-up messages, tool output, and tool calls.
Provides FastMCP server templates for serving embedded HTML widgets.
Shows the response metadata structure required for ChatGPT widget rendering.
Documents local development with ngrok and ChatGPT Developer Mode registration.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for widget caching, loading, and connection issues.
Provides a verification script entry point for checking skill file readiness.
limitations: Focuses on ChatGPT Apps with widgets, not standard MCP servers without visual components.
Examples are development templates and need production authentication and deployment hardening.
Widget behavior must still be tested inside ChatGPT because browser previews differ.
Does not provide a complete hosted production deployment pipeline.

use_cases.title: Prototype a widget-based ChatGPT App
use_cases.description: Use the templates to create a FastMCP app that returns embedded widget HTML and structured content.

use_cases.title: Debug ChatGPT widget rendering
use_cases.description: Follow the troubleshooting steps for metadata, MIME type, caching, and tunnel connectivity problems.

use_cases.title: Teach Apps SDK architecture
use_cases.description: Use the diagrams and examples to explain how ChatGPT, widgets, and MCP servers work together.

prompt_templates.scenario: Developer wiring a tool response to a widget
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show the response metadata I need for a ChatGPT widget named dashboard-widget.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot loading failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Widget appears blank or stuck loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to diagnose why my ChatGPT App widget is loading forever and list checks in priority order.

prompt_templates.title: Review an app template for production readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user preparing a development template for deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my ChatGPT App template and identify changes needed before production deployment.

output_examples.input: I need a ChatGPT App that displays a dashboard widget.

The required response metadata for widget rendering.
A local testing sequence using Developer Mode.

output_examples.input: My widget does not update after I changed the HTML.
output: Steps to create a fresh tunnel and app registration.
Checks for MIME type and response metadata.

output_examples.input: How should widget buttons communicate with ChatGPT?
output: Prefer follow-up messages for reliable actions.
Check window.openai APIs before calling them.

best_practices: Use the templates as development starting points and add authentication before public deployment.
Test widgets inside ChatGPT because sandbox behavior differs from a normal browser.
Keep widget HTML self-contained with inline styles and explicit metadata.
anti_patterns: Do not publish a public tunnel with no authentication for real user data.
Do not assume complex browser JavaScript will work reliably inside the widget sandbox.
Do not reuse cached widget URIs when testing major UI changes.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build ChatGPT Apps that combine MCP tools with embedded HTML widgets.

faq.question: Does it cover standard MCP servers?
faq.answer: It focuses on MCP servers that support ChatGPT widgets. Standard MCP-only servers are outside its main scope.

faq.question: Why does it mention ngrok?
faq.answer: ChatGPT needs a reachable HTTPS endpoint during development, and ngrok is used as a local tunnel example.

faq.question: Can I use the templates in production?
faq.answer: Use them as a starting point only. Add authentication, deployment controls, and safer process management first.

faq.question: What is the most important widget metadata?
faq.answer: Tool responses must include the openai.com/widget metadata with an embedded widget resource.

faq.question: Why should I test inside ChatGPT?
faq.answer: The widget sandbox provides window.openai APIs and behavior that normal browser previews do not reproduce.
